Print_Text_RadioSurvivor_NoteWalt_info:
STATION LOG

2 AM - a voice from across the river. Calls himself Walt. Says he got out.
%1 MHz. Answers any hour, day or night. Walkie or ham set, push to talk.
He can't come get anyone. But he talks. That's something.
Print_Text_RadioSurvivor_NoteDarlene_inf:
PATIENT CARE INSTRUCTIONS

Nurse on the radio - Darlene. %1 MHz.
Mornings 7 to 10, evenings 4 to 7.
Wounds, fever, pills: ask her. She won't say where she is.
Print_Text_RadioSurvivor_NoteCody_info:
KENTUCKY ARMY NATIONAL GUARD - LOOKOUT NOTICE

SUBJECT: HASKINS, Cody, Specialist.
STATUS: absent without leave from his post at the Esther Kinsella bridge checkpoint. Armed. Carries a field radio.
Believed to transmit on shortwave, %1 MHz, between 2200 and 0300 hours.
All stations: monitor this frequency and report any traffic. Do not answer.

Handwritten in the margin: "He talks sense. Listen at night."
Print_Text_RadioSurvivor_NoteGus_info: Got something to sell? Ask for GUS on the marine band: %1 MHz.\nBefore dawn, 3 to 6.\nCash, jewelry, papers. Talk straight. No begging.
Print_Text_RadioSurvivor_NoteNightOwl_in:
THE NIGHT OWL - Knox County is still on the air

Every evening, 7 to 10 PM, on %1 MHz.
Confirmed news. The names that reach us. A little music.
Any radio can listen. Call in on a walkie.

Keep your radio on. Keep your head down.

Print_Text_RadioSurvivor_OutsideNews_lea: ARMY PUSHES THE FENCE FURTHER ALONG THE RIVER

Soldiers have extended the fence line along the Kentucky bank. Boats stay banned on the Ohio below the Clark Memorial bridge. On the Indiana side, river towns live with searchlights all night and a patrol boat every hour.
REFUGEE CAMPS FULL IN SOUTHERN INDIANA

Tents and school gyms are full from Jeffersonville to Madison. Families who got out before the fence went up still wait for word of their relatives. The Red Cross asks for blankets, diapers and drinking water.
WASHINGTON ARGUES, THE FENCE STAYS
Hearings drag on in Congress about who knew what, and when. Officials repeat that the exclusion zone is holding. Nobody on the panel would say when the fence comes down.
HOME VIDEO FROM INSIDE THE ZONE ON TELEVISION
A network aired shaky home video said to come from inside Knox County. The government calls it unverified. The station phones rang all night with viewers asking about their families.
NIGHT CURFEW IN EVERY RIVER COUNTY
Indiana has extended its curfew to every county facing the Ohio. State police turn cars back at the bridges. Anyone caught on the water after dark risks arrest, or worse.
RATIONING IN THE STORES
Supermarkets limit canned food, batteries and bottled water to one bag per family. Lines start before dawn in Evansville and New Albany. Most gas stations are dry by noon.
DOCTORS STILL HAVE NO ANSWER
Federal health officials still cannot name the cause of the outbreak. No vaccine, no treatment. Hospitals near the fence now turn away anyone with a bite, and guards stand at their doors.
CANDLES ON THE INDIANA BANK
Every Sunday evening, people gather on the shore with candles and photographs. They look at the dark side of the river for a long time. The soldiers let them pray, then send them home.
SHOTS ON THE RIVER AT NIGHT
Witnesses describe gunfire on the water after dark. The Army says warning shots only, and only at boats that will not stop. Fishermen have pulled their boats out of the river.
MARKETS SLIDE, PRICES CLIMB
Stocks fell again on Wall Street as the news from Kentucky spread. Insurers refuse every claim tied to the zone. Fuel and food cost more every week, and nobody expects it to stop.
Print_Text_RadioSurvivor_OutsideNews_bri: Shelters full
Animal shelters in Clark County are full of dogs left behind by the families who fled.
Baseball
The Reds play on, to half-empty stands. Fans say nobody feels like cheering.
Schools
Schools near the river may not open in the fall: their gyms still house the refugees.
Telephone
Calls to Kentucky end in a recorded message. The phone company blames damaged lines.
Mail
The Post Office holds every letter addressed inside the zone. The sacks pile up in Indianapolis.
Blood drive
Hospitals ask for blood donors. In Indianapolis the line goes around the block.
Gun shops
Gun shops across Indiana report empty shelves and waiting lists.
Ferry closed
The last ferry on the Ohio has stopped running until further notice.
Rumors
Police warn against rumors of other outbreaks in Tennessee and Ohio. None is confirmed.
Missing persons
A missing persons office has opened in Jeffersonville. Its walls are covered with photographs.
Fishing banned
Fishing is banned along the Indiana bank until further notice. The fines are steep.
Boats
Used boats sell for three times their price. The sheriff seizes any boat launched at night.
